proposals.evidence: Platts p. 1240 gives hawā “air, wind” through Persian from Arabic. The wind/air sense selects this loan family, distinct from the separately listed Arabic desire homonym. Existing Hindi hava “wind” (kannauji[p. 66]) supplies an attested provisional donor. Its locality is the attestation site; the historical lending locality and possible intervening Indo-Aryan language remain unknown. The borrowed edge is saved under the user’s explicit preference to link supported families despite unresolved cross-IA transmission.
